chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Does the one in Ihram brush his teeth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said, 'And if he bleeds, does he brush his teeth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, it is from the Sunnah.' And it is also reported that he should not bleed.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.يَسْتَدْمِي: Causes bleeding (specifically from gums while brushing)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram brush their teeth if it causes bleeding?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that the permissibility of using Siwak during Ihram is rooted in its status as a Sunnah act of purification, which remains valid even if it causes minor bleeding (dam). The apparent contradiction with the report 'he does not cause bleeding' is resolved by scholars as distinguishing between the general permissibility of the act and the recommended precaution (istihbab) to avoid unnecessary harm, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of reconciling seemingly conflicting reports through contextual nuance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The one in Ihraam, can he brush his teeth?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘Supposing he brushes his teeth habitually (frequently)?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, it is from the Sunnah’. And it is reported that that he should not bleed.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is in the state of Ihram; if he can brush his teeth. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is of the Sunnah.’ It is also narrated that one must not make his teeth bleed.”
